walkthroughs.body_html: Siddhartha Gautama was born a prince in what is now Nepal around 500 BCE. After seeing suffering in the world, he left his palace, meditated, and gained enlightenment under a Bodhi tree. He became the Buddha — 'the awakened one' — and taught others for 45 years.
The Buddha taught the Four Noble Truths: 1) Life involves suffering (dukkha). 2) Suffering is caused by craving and clinging. 3) Suffering can end. 4) The way to end it is the Eightfold Path.

The Eightfold Path is eight ways of living: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness and right concentration. Following it leads to Nirvana — the end of suffering.

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.

Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
